title_en: Ace Europe Group Co., Ltd. v. Lianyungang Mingri International Shipping Co., Ltd. and Shanghai Mingri International Shipping Co., Ltd. — dispute over voyage charter party contract
ruling_gist_en: The parties to a voyage charter party are the owner and the charterer. Where a voyage charter party contains explicit provisions, the owner shall perform its obligations in accordance with the voyage charter party and shall also perform the obligations stipulated in Articles 47 and 49 of the Maritime Code of the People's Republic of China. In the absence of provisions or differing provisions in the voyage charter party, the rights and obligations of the owner and the charterer shall be governed by the provisions of Chapter IV of the Maritime Code of the People's Republic of China concerning the rights and obligations of the carrier and the shipper under a contract of carriage of goods by sea. When a charterer makes a claim under the voyage charter party, in accordance with the principle of privity of contract, the owner under the voyage charter party shall bear the corresponding liability. The actual carrier is not a party to the legal relationship of the voyage charter party, and a claim for compensation by the charterer against the actual carrier under the voyage charter party lacks legal basis.

full_text_en:
ACE European Group Limited v. Lianyungang Mingri International Shipping Co., Ltd. and Shanghai Mingri International Shipping Co., Ltd. — dispute over voyage charter party

【Ruling Summary】

The parties to a voyage charter party are the shipowner (charterer) and the charterer (shipper). Where the voyage charter party contains explicit terms, the shipowner shall perform its obligations in accordance with the voyage charter party and also fulfill the obligations set forth in Articles 47 and 49 of the Maritime Code of the People's Republic of China. Where the voyage charter party contains no provisions or no differing provisions, the rights and obligations of the shipowner and the charterer shall be governed by the provisions of Chapter IV of the Maritime Code of the People's Republic of China concerning the rights and obligations of the carrier and the shipper under a contract of carriage of goods by sea. If the charterer files a claim under the voyage charter party, the shipowner under the voyage charter party shall bear the corresponding liability in accordance with the principle of privity of contract. An actual carrier is not a party to the legal relationship under the voyage charter party, and the charterer's claim for compensation against the actual carrier under the voyage charter party lacks legal basis.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2011) Min Ti Zi No. 16

Re-Applicant (Defendant at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Lianyungang Mingri International Shipping Co., Ltd. Domicile: Room 201, Unit 1, No. 11 Bianhu East Road, Economic and Technological Development Zone, Lianyungang City, Jiangsu Province, People's Republic of China.

Legal Representative: Lu Hong, Chairman of the Board of Directors.

Agent ad litem: Wang Pengnan, lawyer of Liaoning Pengrun Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Wang, lawyer of Liaoning Pengrun Law Firm.

Re-Respondent (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): ACE European Group Limited. Domicile: ACE Building, 100 Leadenhall Street, London, United Kingdom.

Legal Representative: Roland Peter Murray, Director of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Li Zengli, lawyer of Shanghai Yaoliang Law Firm.

Defendant at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance: Shanghai Mingri International Shipping Co., Ltd. Domicile: Unit J, Room 403, No. 1325 Mudanjiang Road, Baoshan District, Shanghai City, People's Republic of China.

Legal Representative: Sun Liang, Chairman of the Board of Directors.

Agent ad litem: Li Yingchun, lawyer of Beijing Dacheng Law Firm, Shanghai Branch.

Agent ad litem: Zhou Yin, lawyer of Beijing Dacheng Law Firm, Shanghai Branch.

In the dispute over voyage charter party between Lianyungang Mingri International Shipping Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Lianyungang Mingri) and ACE European Group Limited (hereinafter referred to as ACE), and Shanghai Mingri International Shipping Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Shanghai Mingri), Lianyungang Mingri, dissatisfied with the civil judgment (2010) Hu Gao Min Si (Hai) Zhong Zi No. 71 rendered by the Shanghai High People's Court, filed an application for retrial with this Court. This Court, by civil ruling (2010) Min Shen Zi No. 1491 dated December 30, 2010, decided to initiate a retrial of this case. This Court lawfully formed a collegial panel and held a public hearing on February 21, 2011. The agents ad litem of Lianyungang Mingri, Wang Pengnan and Wang, the agent ad litem of ACE, Li Zengli, and the agents ad litem of Shanghai Mingri, Li Yingchun and Zhou Yin, appeared in court. This case is now concluded.

On January 22, 2009, ACE filed a lawsuit with the Shanghai Maritime Court, alleging that: On January 27, 2006, as a co-insurer together with eight other insurers, it issued insurance policy No. T099281 to the insureds Manuchar N.V. and Manuchar Steel N.V., covering goods transported worldwide by all modes of transport, with coverage including all risks, war risks, etc. In early November of the same year, Manuchar N.V. and Manuchar Steel N.V. reached a voyage charter party for the vessel "Tongcheng" with Shanghai Mingri via email, agreeing that Shanghai Mingri would provide part of the cargo space of the "Tongcheng" to carry the goods consigned by Manuchar N.V. and Manuchar Steel N.V. Pursuant to this contract, Shanghai Mingri issued thirteen sets of clean bills of lading, and ACE issued corresponding insurance certificates for the goods under each set of bills of lading in accordance with insurance policy T099281. On January 22, 2007, the "Tongcheng" issued a general average declaration. Inspection revealed that the cargo on board was severely damaged. In accordance with the insurance policy, ACE paid compensation to the insured and obtained subrogation rights. The cargo damage was caused by the "Tongcheng" being unseaworthy and the carrier's failure to properly care for the cargo. Shanghai Mingri entered into the voyage charter party with Manuchar N.V. and Manuchar Steel N.V. and issued the bills of lading. Lianyungang Mingri was the bareboat charterer of the "Tongcheng" and actually operated the vessel. Accordingly, ACE requested a judgment that Lianyungang Mingri and Shanghai Mingri be jointly and severally liable for the cargo loss.

Shanghai Mingri and Lianyungang Mingri answered that: The voyage charter party was entered into between Shanghai Mingri and the Beijing office of Manuchar N.V.; no voyage charter party relationship existed between Manuchar N.V. and Manuchar Steel N.V. on one side and Shanghai Mingri on the other; rather, it was a contract of carriage of goods by sea evidenced by the bills of lading. The trade terms of the goods were CIF, and the risk of loss passed to the buyer of the goods when the goods crossed the ship's rail at the port of loading. As the sellers of the goods, Manuchar N.V. and Manuchar Steel N.V. had no insurable interest at the time of the damage. ACE's payment to them lacked contractual and legal basis and could not lawfully obtain subrogation rights. The cargo damage was caused by a maritime accident, for which Shanghai Mingri and Lianyungang Mingri were not liable under law. The evidence provided by ACE was insufficient to prove the extent and scope of the damage, and the amount claimed was unreasonable. ACE's lawsuit was time-barred. Accordingly, they requested that all of ACE's claims be dismissed.

The Shanghai Maritime Court found the following facts at first instance: From October to November 2006, the Beijing office of Manuchar N.V., authorized by Manuchar N.V. and Manuchar Steel N.V. to negotiate and enter into a voyage charter party for the vessel "Tongcheng", entered into a voyage charter party with Shanghai Mingri via email. To perform the contract, Shanghai Mingri issued thirteen sets of bills of lading. According to the vessel's certificate of ownership registration, Lianyungang Mingri was the bareboat charterer of the "Tongcheng". The "Tongcheng" had obtained ship certificates issued by China Classification Society, valid until June 2009. On January 27, 2006, ACE, as insurer together with JEAN VERHEYEN N.V., FORTIS CORPORATE INSURANCE N.V., AXA BELGIUM S.A./N.V., B.D.M. N.V. (formerly MINERVA UNDERWRITERS N.V.), HDI-GERLING VERZEKERINGEN N.V., CATLIN BELGIUM, NATEUS N.V., and AVERO BELGIUM INSURANCE N.V., jointly issued insurance policy No. T099281 200601, covering the risk of goods transported worldwide by Manuchar N.V. and its affiliates from February 1, 2006, on an all risks basis, with the affiliates including Manuchar Steel N.V., and issued separate insurance certificates.

On January 22, 2007, the chief officer of the "Tongcheng" issued a general average declaration. From February 20 to 28, AIMU Marine Survey and Management Co., as Lloyd's agent, issued a report on the temporary repair specifications of the "Tongcheng", pointing out various defects. On April 12, HaiShang Marine Surveyors Co., Ltd. issued a cargo survey report, which stated that the lower hold of No. 2 hatch of the "Tongcheng" had flooded, causing damage to the cargo in question, and that the cause of the damage should be attributed to the vessel's overall poor condition and unseaworthiness. The report also determined that, after the occurrence of the cargo damage, the carrier failed to properly care for the cargo. On May 21, Shanghai Mingri submitted an application to Shanghai Customs for abandonment of the damaged cargo from the "Tongcheng". Ultimately, among the thirteen consignments, the goods under bills of lading TCP010, TRD011, LD04, LD13, and LD15 were total losses and were not taken delivery of by the consignees. After the "Tongcheng" underwent permanent repairs at Shanghai port, the goods that were partially short-delivered or damaged were re-shipped, and Shanghai Mingri's agent at the port of discharge re-issued bills of lading for those goods, which were delivered to the respective consignees in July 2007. Manuchar N.V. and Manuchar Steel N.V. also re-issued partial invoices for the goods based on the damage and shortage. After inspecting the shortage and damage at the port of discharge, the insurance agent considered that: the goods under bill of lading TRD013 were short-delivered by USD 28,082.89; goods under TRD015 were short-delivered and damaged by USD 18,988; goods under TRD016 were short-delivered by USD 25,360.09; goods under LD05 were short-delivered and damaged by USD 34,735.67; goods under LD06 were damaged by USD 57,087.27; goods under LD07 were damaged by USD 22,989.24; goods under LD22 were damaged by USD 4,905.85; goods under TRD008 were a constructive total loss. According to the cargo invoices, the freight for the goods under TRD008 was USD 16,215.00; the FOB value of goods under TRD013 was USD 41,200.80, with freight of USD 1,665.00 and insurance premium of USD 428.66; the FOB value of goods under TRD015 was USD 91,000.00, with freight of USD 3,000.00 and insurance premium of USD 940.00; the FOB value of goods under TRD016 was USD 76,875.00, with freight of USD 2,250.00 and insurance premium of USD 791.25; the FOB value of goods under LD05 was USD 62,115.48, with freight of USD 2,875.77 and insurance premium of USD 649.91; the FOB value of goods under LD06 was USD 97,327.88, with freight of USD 4,301.49 and insurance premium of USD 1,016.29; the FOB value of goods under LD07 was USD 243,739.17, with freight of USD 13,165.83 and insurance premium of USD 2,569.05; the FOB value of goods under LD22 was USD 30,672.99, with freight of USD 1,202.91 and insurance premium of USD 318.76. According to the customs declarations, the FOB value of goods under TRD008 was USD 430,000.00; the FOB value of goods under TRD013 was USD 31,912.50; the FOB value of goods under TRD015 was USD 77,100.00; the FOB value of goods under TRD016 was USD 65,625.00; the FOB value of goods under LD05 was USD 25,875.00; the FOB value of goods under LD06 was USD 30,153.00; the FOB value of goods under LD07 was USD 199,020.00; and the FOB value of goods under LD22 was USD 24,860.14. Shanghai Mingri confirmed that Manuchar N.V. and Manuchar Steel N.V. had paid all freight for the thirteen consignments.

After the occurrence of the cargo damage, the nine co-insurers including ACE paid insurance compensation of USD 956,459.61 to Manuchar N.V. and paid brokerage commissions of USD 9,656.85 to the insurance broker; they paid insurance compensation of USD 402,232.77 to Manuchar Steel N.V. and paid brokerage commissions of USD 4,062.95 to the insurance broker. Since ACE's share of the risk in the co-insurance was 5%, it actually paid USD 68,620.61 to Manuchar N.V. and Manuchar Steel N.V. Manuchar N.V. and Manuchar Steel N.V. issued receipts upon receiving the compensation and also issued letters of subrogation, confirming the transfer of the claim rights for the cargo damage to the nine co-insurers.

The Shanghai Maritime Court held at first instance that this case was a dispute over a voyage charter party involving foreign elements. All parties expressed their willingness to apply the laws of the People's Republic of China, so it was determined that the laws of the People's Republic of China would govern the case.

I. Regarding the dispute over the legal relationship between Manuchar N.V. and Manuchar Steel N.V. on the one hand and Lianyungang Mingri and Shanghai Mingri on the other.

The court of first instance held that the business registration materials of the Beijing office of Manuchar N.V. showed that it was an agency of Manuchar N.V. The execution of the voyage charter party with Shanghai Mingri indicated the establishment of a voyage charter party relationship between Manuchar N.V. and Shanghai Mingri. The letter of authorization proved that the Beijing office of Manuchar N.V. also accepted the mandate of Manuchar Steel N.V. to enter into the voyage charter party with Shanghai Mingri. The bills of lading issued by Shanghai Mingri explicitly indicated that the shippers were Manuchar N.V. or Manuchar Steel N.V., and freight was collected from Manuchar N.V. and Manuchar Steel N.V. Therefore, it could be determined that a voyage charter party relationship also existed between Manuchar Steel N.V. and Shanghai Mingri. Lianyungang Mingri, as the bareboat charterer of the vessel involved, should be deemed the actual carrier of the cargo.

II. Regarding the dispute over whether Manuchar N.V. and Manuchar Steel N.V. had an insurable interest in the cargo and whether the subrogation right was lawful.

The court of first instance held that this case was a subrogation dispute arising from a voyage charter party. The main issue was whether the subrogated persons, Manuchar N.V. and Manuchar Steel N.V., had the right to sue for the cargo damage and whether they suffered losses. As parties to the voyage charter party and the shippers recorded in the bills of lading, Manuchar N.V. and Manuchar Steel N.V. naturally had the right to claim compensation after the cargo damage occurred. Among the thirteen consignments, five were determined to be total losses, and the consignees did not take delivery of the goods. Manuchar N.V. and Manuchar Steel N.V. always held the original full sets of bills of lading for those five consignments and thus suffered losses for those goods. The other eight consignments suffered varying degrees of shortage and damage. The consignees confirmed that they had not paid the purchase price for the short-delivered or damaged goods, and the corresponding claim rights should belong to Manuchar N.V. and Manuchar Steel N.V. Accordingly, Manuchar N.V. and Manuchar Steel N.V. suffered losses for those eight consignments. As the insurer, ACE paid insurance compensation and obtained the letters of subrogation issued by Manuchar N.V. and Manuchar Steel N.V., thereby lawfully acquiring the subrogation right and was entitled to claim compensation from the party responsible for the cargo damage.

III. Regarding the dispute over the cause of the cargo damage and whether Lianyungang Mingri and Shanghai Mingri should bear liability for compensation.

The court of first instance held that the cargo in question was non-containerized cargo, and the carrier's period of responsibility ran from the time the goods were loaded on board until the time they were discharged. The cargo damage occurred during the carrier's period of responsibility, and the carrier should bear liability for compensation unless it could prove the existence of statutory exemptions. The technical appraisal report provided by Lianyungang Mingri only suggested possibilities and was not supported by evidence, nor did it prove that the accident constituted force majeure. The ship certificates of the "Tongcheng" provided by Lianyungang Mingri were still valid before the vessel left Busan port, but the certificates could not directly prove the causal relationship between the cargo damage that occurred during the voyage and the absence of negligence by the carrier in the management of the vessel and cargo. Accordingly, Shanghai Mingri, as the shipowner under the voyage charter party, should bear liability for compensation. Lianyungang Mingri, as the actual carrier, should bear joint and several liability with Shanghai Mingri for compensation.

IV. Regarding the dispute over the basis and reasonableness of the amount of loss.

The court of first instance held that the actual value of the goods should be determined by the customs declaration records. Among the thirteen consignments, five were total losses, one (under bill of lading TRD008) was a constructive total loss, and the other seven suffered partial shortages or damage. According to the law, the actual value of the goods is calculated as the value of the goods at the time of loading plus insurance premium plus freight. The total actual loss of the thirteen consignments was USD 921,899.50. ACE's share of the cargo risk in the co-insurance was 5%, so its actual loss should be USD 46,094.98. As to its request to calculate the loss at 110% of the insured value, the court of first instance did not support it due to lack of basis. Lianyungang Mingri argued that some of the totally lost goods still had residual value, but the court of first instance did not accept this argument because Lianyungang Mingri failed to provide valid evidence. Regarding interest losses, they were incidental losses caused by Lianyungang Mingri and Shanghai Mingri's delay in performing their debts and could be supported. However, since no evidence was provided that ACE had previously requested compensation from Lianyungang Mingri and Shanghai Mingri, and no corresponding loan basis was provided, the interest loss should be calculated at the People's Bank of China's corporate USD demand deposit rate for the corresponding period.

V. Regarding the dispute over whether the lawsuit was time-barred.

The court of first instance held that the statute of limitations for claims under a voyage charter party is two years. In this case, due to the occurrence of the maritime accident, the chief officer of the "Tongcheng" issued a general average declaration on January 22, 2007. That date could be deemed as the date when ACE knew or should have known that its rights were infringed, and should be the starting point for the statute of limitations. ACE submitted its complaint on January 22, 2009. The court of first instance notified ACE that the complaint needed to be corrected, and ACE then submitted the corrected complaint on March 3. Therefore, the date of filing was January 22, 2009, which did not exceed the statute of limitations. As for Lianyungang Mingri, as the actual carrier, the two-year statute of limitations for torts applied, running from the date when the claimant knew or should have known that its rights were infringed. Therefore, the lawsuit against Lianyungang Mingri also did not exceed the statute of limitations.

In summary, the Shanghai Maritime Court, in accordance with Article 135 and Article 137 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China, Article 46(1), Article 48, Article 55(1) and (2), Article 63, Article 92, Article 94(2), Article 252(1), Article 257(2), and Article 269 of the Maritime Code of the People's Republic of China, and Article 64(1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, ruled: 1. Shanghai Mingri and Lianyungang Mingri shall jointly and severally compensate ACE for cargo loss of USD 46,094.98 plus interest losses; 2. All other claims of ACE are dismissed.

Shanghai Tomorrow, Lianyungang Tomorrow, and ACE Company all appealed against the first-instance judgment to the Shanghai High People's Court.

Shanghai Tomorrow appealed on the grounds that: 1. Marusha Company and Marusha Steel Company were not the contracting parties reached through email; the authorization letter in dispute was not genuine and was not issued before the conclusion of the voyage charter party; it should be held that a contractual relationship was established between Marusha Company's Beijing Office and Shanghai Tomorrow. The contract in dispute was in the nature of a slot charter. The relationship between Marusha Company and Marusha Steel Company on one side and Shanghai Tomorrow on the other was a contract of carriage of goods by sea evidenced by bills of lading. 2. Marusha Company and Marusha Steel Company had no insurable interest in the cargo in dispute; the subrogation right in dispute was not legally acquired; the cargo in dispute was on CIF terms, and the risk of loss of the cargo had passed to the buyer once the cargo crossed the ship's rail. 3. The technical appraisal report in dispute indicated that an accident occurred during the voyage; the vessel "Tongcheng" was seaworthy before and at the commencement of the voyage in dispute; the cargo damage was caused by an accident; Lianyungang Tomorrow and Shanghai Tomorrow should be exonerated from liability in accordance with law. 4. The cargo in dispute had residual value. 5. The relationship between Marusha Company and Marusha Steel Company on one side and Shanghai Tomorrow on the other was a contract of carriage of goods by sea, with a statute of limitations of one year; the lawsuit in this case had already exceeded the statute of limitations. On these grounds, it requested the court of second instance to set aside the first-instance judgment and instead dismiss all claims of ACE Company; all litigation costs in this case to be borne by ACE Company.

Lianyungang Tomorrow appealed on the grounds that: 1. Marusha Company and Marusha Steel Company were not the contracting parties reached through email; the subject of the contract in dispute was the Beijing Office of Marusha Company and Shanghai Tomorrow. The authorization letter in dispute was not genuine and was not issued before the conclusion of the voyage charter party; on November 3, 2006, Shanghai Tomorrow did not know that the Beijing Office of Marusha Company was acting on behalf of Marusha Company and Marusha Steel Company; it should be held that a contractual relationship was established between the Beijing Office of Marusha Company and Shanghai Tomorrow. The contract in dispute was in the nature of a slot charter. The relationship between Marusha Company and Marusha Steel Company on one side and Shanghai Tomorrow on the other was a contract of carriage of goods by sea evidenced by bills of lading; Lianyungang Tomorrow was the actual carrier and had no legal relationship with the charterer under the slot charter. 2. Marusha Company and Marusha Steel Company had no insurable interest in the cargo in dispute; the subrogation right in dispute was not legally acquired; the cargo in dispute was on CIF terms, and the risk of loss of the cargo had passed to the buyer once the cargo crossed the ship's rail; Marusha Company and Marusha Steel Company had no insurable interest at the time of the accident. 3. The technical appraisal report in dispute indicated that an accident occurred during the voyage; the vessel "Tongcheng" was seaworthy before and at the commencement of the voyage in dispute; the cargo damage in dispute was caused by an accident; Lianyungang Tomorrow and Shanghai Tomorrow should be exonerated from liability in accordance with law. 4. The cargo in dispute had residual value. 5. The relationship between Marusha Company and Marusha Steel Company on one side and Shanghai Tomorrow on the other was a contract of carriage of goods by sea; the lawsuit in this case had already exceeded the statute of limitations. On these grounds, it requested the court of second instance to set aside the first-instance judgment and instead dismiss all claims of ACE Company; all litigation costs in this case to be borne by ACE Company.

ACE Company appealed on the grounds that: the quantity of cargo under bill of lading TRD008 was 1,000 tons; the actual loss of cargo should be USD 530,154.20. On this ground, it requested the court of second instance to amend the judgment to order Lianyungang Tomorrow and Shanghai Tomorrow to jointly and severally compensate it for cargo loss of USD 50,291.94 and interest loss; all litigation costs in this case to be borne by Lianyungang Tomorrow and Shanghai Tomorrow.

Shanghai Tomorrow argued in defense that: the vessel in dispute was seaworthy before and at the commencement of the voyage; the expert appraisal report could prove that the vessel's water ingress was caused by an accident; the accident in dispute was caused by a latent defect in the vessel in dispute; Shanghai Tomorrow should be exonerated from liability for the cargo damage in dispute.

Lianyungang Tomorrow argued in defense that: the actual carrier arises together with the carrier; the provisions of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China on statute of limitations should not apply. The concept of actual carrier exists only in the relationship of a contract of carriage of goods by sea evidenced by a bill of lading, and has no relationship with the voyage charter party in this case. Regarding the cause of cargo damage and exemption from liability, it agreed with the statement of Shanghai Tomorrow. Lianyungang Tomorrow should not bear joint and several liability for compensation.

ACE Company argued in defense that: there was a voyage charter party relationship between it and Shanghai Tomorrow; Lianyungang Tomorrow was the actual carrier; the first-instance judgment ordering Lianyungang Tomorrow and Shanghai Tomorrow to bear joint and several liability was in accordance with law. There was insufficient evidence to prove that the accident in dispute was caused by an accident; Lianyungang Tomorrow also did not specify the cause of the accident. The residual value of the cargo in dispute was not supported by corresponding documents.

Upon trial at the second instance, the Shanghai High People's Court held that, based on the existing evidence, the facts found in the first-instance judgment were clear and could be confirmed.

The court of second instance held that this case is a dispute over a voyage charter party involving foreign elements. Since all parties in this case chose to apply the laws of the People's Republic of China to resolve the dispute in question, the laws of the People's Republic of China may be applied as the governing law for resolving the dispute in this case.

I. Regarding the nature of the contract in dispute, the legal status of each party, and the statute of limitations.

The Beijing Office of Marusha Company and Shanghai Tomorrow concluded the contract in dispute via email. In form, it used the wording of a charter party for the vessel "Tongcheng"; in content, it covered the vessel name, quantity, loading and discharging ports, laydays, freight, demurrage, etc., and possessed the characteristics of a voyage charter party. Although a bill of lading was issued by the carrier under the voyage charter party in dispute, the Maritime Code of the People's Republic of China does not prohibit the issuance of bills of lading by the carrier under a voyage charter party; the fact that the carrier issued a bill of lading does not affect the establishment of the voyage charter party in this case. The first-instance judgment correctly held that the contract in dispute was a voyage charter party. The grounds of appeal of Lianyungang Tomorrow and Shanghai Tomorrow that the contract in dispute was a slot charter or a contract of carriage of goods by sea lacked basis and were not accepted. The authorization letter in dispute indicated that the Beijing Office of Marusha Company, as an agency of Marusha Company, concluded the contract in dispute and had obtained authorization from Marusha Company and Marusha Steel Company; therefore, it could be confirmed that a voyage charter party relationship was established among Marusha Company, Marusha Steel Company, and Shanghai Tomorrow, with Lianyungang Tomorrow being the actual carrier. According to law, the limitation period for claims under a voyage charter party is two years, and the limitation period for claims against the actual carrier is also two years. The court of first instance took January 22, 2007, the date of issuance of the general average declaration, as the starting point for the limitation period and held that the lawsuit in this case did not exceed the statute of limitations, which was in accordance with the law and was affirmed.

II. Regarding whether the subrogation right in dispute was lawful.

The first-instance found that, among the thirteen lots of cargo in dispute, for the five lots of total loss, the consignees did not take delivery, and Marusha Company and Marusha Steel Company always held one set of three original bills of lading; for the other eight lots of cargo with varying degrees of shortage and damage, the consignees declared that they had not paid the purchase price for the short and damaged cargo, and the corresponding claim rights should belong to Marusha Company and Marusha Steel Company; therefore, Marusha Company and Marusha Steel Company, as shippers, had the right to claim. ACE Company, as the insurer, after paying insurance compensation to Marusha Company and Marusha Steel Company and obtaining the relevant letter of subrogation, lawfully acquired the subrogation right.

III. Regarding the cause of cargo damage and whether Lianyungang Tomorrow and Shanghai Tomorrow could be exonerated.

Under a non-containerized cargo contract, the carrier's period of responsibility runs from the time the cargo is loaded on board until the time it is discharged. The cargo damage in dispute occurred within the carrier's period of responsibility. Shanghai Tomorrow and Lianyungang Tomorrow, claiming exemption from liability, should bear the corresponding burden of proof. From the existing evidence, it was insufficient to prove that there was indeed a ground for the carrier to be exonerated from liability; therefore, Shanghai Tomorrow and Lianyungang Tomorrow should bear joint and several liability for compensation for the cargo damage in dispute.

IV. Regarding the amount of loss.

Both Shanghai Tomorrow and Lianyungang Tomorrow claimed that part of the cargo in dispute still had residual value, but they did not provide effective evidence to prove it; therefore, this claim was difficult to accept. Regarding ACE Company's argument that the actual loss of cargo under bill of lading TRD008 should be USD 530,154.20, the court of second instance held that the first-instance judgment, based on ACE Company's own statement in the first instance and in combination with the customs declaration numbers for the cargo in dispute provided by ACE Company and materials issued by the customs authorities, made a determination of the amount of cargo damage under bill of lading TRD008. ACE Company, in the second instance, sought to overturn its statement made in the first instance but did not provide sufficient evidence; it should accordingly bear the adverse consequences.

In summary, the appeal requests of Shanghai Tomorrow, Lianyungang Tomorrow, and ACE Company all lacked factual and legal basis. The first-instance judgment had clear findings of fact and correct application of law, and should be affirmed. Pursuant to Article 153, paragraph 1, subparagraph (1) and Article 158 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the judgment was: appeal dismissed, original judgment affirmed.

Lianyungang Tomorrow, dissatisfied with the original judgment, filed an application for retrial with this Court, alleging: 1. The original judgment erred in the application of law. The original judgment treated Lianyungang Tomorrow as the actual carrier in the legal relationship of the voyage charter party, which was clearly a fundamental error in the application of law. The parties to a voyage charter party are only the shipowner and the charterer; the actual carrier exists only in the legal relationship of a contract of carriage of goods by sea evidenced by a bill of lading; in any case, the statute of limitations for claims against the actual carrier should be one year from the date of delivery or the date when the goods should have been delivered. The original judgment found it to be two years from the date when the right was known or should have been known, which was also a clear fundamental error in the application of law. 2. The original judgment had obvious errors in the factual findings regarding the cause of cargo damage and grounds for exemption. In this case, the vessel "Tongcheng" was seaworthy before and at the commencement of the voyage in dispute, and the shipowner had the right to claim exemption; the applicant for retrial has new evidence sufficient to overturn the erroneous findings of the original judgment on the cause of cargo damage and grounds for exemption. Lianyungang Tomorrow requested this Court to set aside the original judgment, amend the judgment to dismiss all claims of the respondent, and order all litigation costs in this case to be borne by the respondent.

ACE Company argued in defense: 1. This case is a dispute over a voyage charter party. Shanghai Tomorrow and Lianyungang Tomorrow, as co-shipowners, should bear joint and several liability for the damage to the cargo in dispute, with a statute of limitations of two years. 2. Lianyungang Tomorrow is the actual carrier under the Maritime Code of the People's Republic of China. Lianyungang Tomorrow's argument that there is no actual carrier in a voyage charter party legal relationship and its responsibilities and obligations has no legal basis. The law does not restrict the application of the concept of actual carrier; the liability of the actual carrier is statutory, and Lianyungang Tomorrow should bear joint and several liability for compensation with Shanghai Tomorrow. The statute of limitations for claims by Marusha Company against Lianyungang Tomorrow as the actual carrier should be the same as the statute of limitations for claims against Shanghai Tomorrow as the contractual carrier, i.e., two years from the date when the right was known or should have been known, in accordance with the special provisions of the Maritime Code of the People's Republic of China on the statute of limitations for disputes over voyage charter parties. 3. If Lianyungang Tomorrow is found not to be the actual carrier or co-shipowner under the voyage charter party in dispute, then in the case where Lianyungang Tomorrow breached its statutory duty to properly care for the cargo, resulting in loss or damage to the cargo, Lianyungang Tomorrow should be found to be the custodian of the cargo in dispute. Marusha Company, as the cargo owner, could claim against Lianyungang Tomorrow based on tort under the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China, with a statute of limitations of two years. The creditor's right arising from such tort even has a maritime lien under the Maritime Code of the People's Republic of China. At the same time, Marusha Company could also claim against Shanghai Tomorrow based on the voyage charter party. Both Shanghai Tomorrow and Lianyungang Tomorrow owe compensation liability to Marusha Company, the former based on breach of contract and the latter based on tort. Marusha Company has the right to claim compensation from both Lianyungang Tomorrow and Shanghai Tomorrow jointly. 4. The original judgment correctly held that Lianyungang Tomorrow's claim for exemption could not be sustained. The first and second instance judgments in this case never confirmed that the vessel "Tongcheng" was seaworthy before and at the commencement of the voyage. The documents submitted by Lianyungang Tomorrow in its application for retrial are not new evidence and are insufficient to constitute a legitimate reason for applying for retrial. It requested the dismissal of Lianyungang Tomorrow's application for retrial and the restoration of enforcement of the original judgment.

Shanghai Tomorrow argued in defense: 1. This case is a dispute over a voyage charter party. The party that signed the contract with Shanghai Tomorrow was Marusha Company; the original judgment erred in finding the facts. 2. Under a voyage charter party relationship, there is no concept of actual carrier. 3. According to the spirit of relevant replies of the Supreme People's Court, Lianyungang Tomorrow may serve as a party to the case. 4. Lianyungang Tomorrow should bear civil liability for tort, subject to a statute of limitations of two years. 5. The cargo damage in dispute was caused by a maritime accident due to severe weather at sea; Shanghai Tomorrow has statutory grounds for exemption.

During the retrial, Lianyungang Tomorrow submitted three new pieces of evidence: 1. The "Survey Report" of Mr. Douglas G. Granger, surveyor of Hull & Machinery Surveys (USA); 2. The "Final Report" of Robins Insurance Survey (China) Co., Ltd.; 3. The "Technical Review on the Hull Water Ingress Accident of the Vessel 'Tongcheng'" issued by Professor Wang Jianping of the Navigation College of Dalian Maritime University on August 18, 2010.

With respect to evidence 1, ACE Company raised an objection to its authenticity, arguing that the survey report submitted by Lianyungang Tomorrow was incomplete and lacked a Chinese translation by a qualified translation institution. This document was formed before the second-instance judgment and was not new evidence. The report was prepared for the client's claim and was not relevant to this case. There was no evidence that the surveyor who issued the report had survey qualifications. The report's conclusion merely proposed a possibility and did not constitute a ground for exemption under the Maritime Code of the People's Republic of China. With respect to evidence 2, ACE Company raised no objection to its authenticity but argued that the report was only an assessment of damage, not an expert conclusion on the cause of the maritime accident, could not prove Lianyungang Tomorrow's grounds for exemption, and had no probative value for this case. Moreover, Lianyungang Tomorrow also had no evidence to prove the appraisal qualifications of Robins Insurance Survey (China) Co., Ltd., the issuer of the report. With respect to evidence 3, ACE Company raised no objection to its authenticity but argued that the technical review was written before the second-instance judgment, was not submitted by Lianyungang Tomorrow in the second instance, and this evidence material does not fall within the scope of new evidence under the civil procedure law.

Shanghai Tomorrow raised no objection to the authenticity, legality, or relevance of the three new pieces of evidence submitted by Lianyungang Tomorrow.

Upon examination, this Court found the following with respect to the above evidence materials: Evidence 1: Lianyungang Tomorrow submitted a notarized and authenticated original; its authenticity is affirmed. However, Lianyungang Tomorrow did not submit a Chinese translation by a qualified institution, and ACE Company raised an objection; therefore, the content sought to be proved by this evidence material is not admitted. Evidence 2: This evidence material is an original; its authenticity is affirmed. However, Lianyungang Tomorrow did not submit evidence that the company issuing the report had relevant appraisal qualifications; therefore, the facts sought to be proved by this evidence material are not admitted. Evidence 3: Authenticity is affirmed, but it is only an analysis report on the accident and does not fall within the category of evidence in civil proceedings.

This Court holds that Lianyungang Tomorrow did not submit new evidence sufficient to overturn the facts found in the original judgment. The facts found in the original judgment were clear, and this Court affirms them.

ACE Company is an enterprise legal person registered outside the territory of the People's Republic of China. This case involves foreign legal relations. All parties have no objection to applying the laws of the People's Republic of China to handle this case. The original judgment correctly applied the laws of the People's Republic of China. This case is a dispute over a voyage charter party brought by ACE Company against Shanghai Tomorrow and Lianyungang Tomorrow. The provisions of the Maritime Code of the People's Republic of China shall apply to determine the rights and obligations of the parties.

Based on the focal points of dispute between the parties, this Court holds that the main disputes in this case include the legal status of Lianyungang Tomorrow, the statute of limitations, the cause of cargo damage, and whether there are grounds for exemption from liability for the cargo damage in this case.

I. The legal status of Lianyungang Tomorrow in the charter party dispute of this case.

The original judgment found that a voyage charter party relationship was established among Marusha Company, Marusha Steel Company, and Shanghai Tomorrow, and that Lianyungang Tomorrow was the bareboat charterer of the vessel in dispute; therefore, Lianyungang Tomorrow was the actual carrier. Lianyungang Tomorrow argued that there is no actual carrier in a voyage charter party legal relationship, and the original judgment erroneously determined its legal status. ACE Company argued that Lianyungang Tomorrow, as the bareboat charterer of the vessel "Tongcheng," actually operated the vessel and was the actual carrier. This Court holds that the original judgment improperly determined the legal status of Lianyungang Tomorrow.

This case is a dispute over a voyage charter party. The voyage charter party in dispute was concluded via email between the Beijing Office of Marusha Company, authorized by Marusha Company and Marusha Steel Company, and Shanghai Tomorrow. According to the provisions of the Maritime Code of the People's Republic of China, the parties to a voyage charter party should be the shipowner and the charterer. Therefore, Shanghai Tomorrow, as the shipowner, should bear corresponding liability for the voyage charter party between itself and Marusha Company and Marusha Steel Company. ACE Company, as the cargo insurer, paid insurance compensation to the insured, Marusha Company and Marusha Steel Company, after the cargo damage occurred, and lawfully acquired the right of subrogation. According to the provisions of the Maritime Code of the People's Republic of China, ACE Company's claim against Shanghai Tomorrow, the shipowner under the voyage charter party, should be supported.

Lianyungang Tomorrow is the bareboat charterer of the vessel "Tongcheng" involved in the transport and actually carried the cargo in dispute, but it is not a party to the voyage charter party in dispute. In the lawsuit brought by ACE Company based on the voyage charter party, Lianyungang Tomorrow should not be a party bearing the liability of the shipowner under the voyage charter party. ACE Company's claim that Lianyungang Tomorrow is a co-shipowner of the voyage charter party lacks factual and legal basis.

ACE EUROPEAN GROUP LIMITED argued that Lianyungang Mingri International Shipping Agency Co., Ltd. was the actual carrier under the voyage charter party and should bear joint and several liability with Shanghai Mingri International Ship Services Co., Ltd. This court finds that ACE EUROPEAN GROUP LIMITED's claim has no legal basis. The Maritime Code of the PRC provides for voyage charter parties as special contracts for carriage of goods by sea. Article 94 of that Code provides: "The provisions of Articles 47 and 49 of this Code shall apply to the shipowner under a voyage charter party. The provisions of this Chapter relating to the rights and obligations of the parties to a contract for carriage of goods by sea shall apply to the shipowner and the charterer under a voyage charter party only in the absence of any provisions or any different provisions in the voyage charter party." Therefore, the rights and obligations of the parties to a voyage charter party derive primarily from the contract. Where the voyage charter party contains clear provisions, the shipowner shall perform his obligations in accordance with the voyage charter party and perform the obligations stipulated in Articles 47 and 49 of the Maritime Code. Where the voyage charter party contains no provisions or no different provisions, the rights and obligations between the shipowner and the charterer shall be governed by the provisions of Chapter IV of the Maritime Code, but not all provisions of Chapter IV apply to the parties to a voyage charter party; only the provisions on the rights and obligations of the carrier and the shipper, being the parties to a contract for carriage of goods by sea, apply, and this does not include the provisions on the actual carrier. An actual carrier is a person who, entrusted by the carrier, performs the carriage of goods or part of the carriage, including any other person who performs such carriage under a sub-entrustment. In the legal relationship of maritime cargo carriage evidenced by a bill of lading, the law provides that the carrier's liability extends to the actual carrier, who is not a party to the contract, but the actual carrier is entrusted by the carrier in a contract for carriage of goods by sea, not by the shipowner under a voyage charter party. The actual carrier and its statutory liability are limited to the legal relationship under the bill of lading. Under a contract for carriage of goods by sea evidenced by a bill of lading, a lawful holder of the bill of lading may claim against the carrier and/or the actual carrier the rights stated in the bill of lading. The actual carrier is not a party to the legal relationship of a voyage charter party. In this case, ACE EUROPEAN GROUP LIMITED filed a claim under the voyage charter party. In accordance with the principle of privity of contract, the corresponding liability should be borne by Shanghai Mingri International Ship Services Co., Ltd., the shipowner under the voyage charter party. ACE EUROPEAN GROUP LIMITED's claim that Lianyungang Mingri International Shipping Agency Co., Ltd. is the actual carrier in the legal relationship of the voyage charter party has no legal basis.

2. Regarding the statute of limitations in this case.

This case is a dispute over a voyage charter party. Pursuant to Article 257, paragraph 2 of the Maritime Code of the PRC, the limitation period for claims arising from a voyage charter party is two years, counting from the date on which the claimant knew or should have known that his rights were infringed. Therefore, the limitation period for ACE EUROPEAN GROUP LIMITED's claim against Shanghai Mingri International Ship Services Co., Ltd. is two years, and the trial court's determination in this regard was correct. Since Lianyungang Mingri International Shipping Agency Co., Ltd. is not a party to the voyage charter party in this case, ACE EUROPEAN GROUP LIMITED's claim against it lacks factual and legal basis. Accordingly, this court does not rule on the issue of the statute of limitations raised by Lianyungang Mingri International Shipping Agency Co., Ltd. regarding ACE EUROPEAN GROUP LIMITED's claim for compensation against it.

3. Regarding the cause of the cargo damage and whether there are grounds for exemption from liability.

Shanghai Mingri International Ship Services Co., Ltd. and Lianyungang Mingri International Shipping Agency Co., Ltd. argued that the evidence they submitted could prove that the cargo damage in question was caused by the vessel colliding with an object suspended in the water that was not detectable by radar during navigation, resulting in a crack in the port side shell plating and subsequent water ingress. This court finds that there is insufficient evidence to prove that the cargo damage in question was caused by an accident encountered by the vessel during navigation. The trial court's determination of the cause of the cargo damage incident in question was not improper. Given that Lianyungang Mingri International Shipping Agency Co., Ltd. is not a party to the voyage charter party in this case, ACE EUROPEAN GROUP LIMITED has no right to claim against it. Therefore, this court need not rule on whether Lianyungang Mingri International Shipping Agency Co., Ltd. can be exempted from liability. As for Shanghai Mingri International Ship Services Co., Ltd.'s claim for exemption from liability, the trial court determined that the existing evidence was insufficient to prove the existence of any grounds for exemption from liability. During this court's retrial, no new evidence was presented that could overturn the facts found in the trial court's judgment. Therefore, the trial court's determination that Shanghai Mingri International Ship Services Co., Ltd., as the shipowner under the voyage charter party, should be liable to ACE EUROPEAN GROUP LIMITED for cargo damage compensation was not improper.

In conclusion, this court finds that the trial court's determination that Lianyungang Mingri International Shipping Agency Co., Ltd. was the actual carrier in the legal relationship of the voyage charter party in this case lacks legal basis. Lianyungang Mingri International Shipping Agency Co., Ltd.'s claim that it is not a party to the voyage charter party in this case and should not bear corresponding liability has sufficient evidentiary support and should be upheld. Shanghai Mingri International Ship Services Co., Ltd., as the shipowner under the voyage charter party, should be liable for compensating ACE EUROPEAN GROUP LIMITED for the damage to the insured cargo. Pursuant to Article 46, paragraph 1; Article 48; Article 55, paragraphs 1 and 2; Article 92; Article 94; Article 252, paragraph 1; Article 257, paragraph 2; and Article 269 of the Maritime Code of the PRC; Article 64, paragraph 1; Article 153, paragraph 1, item (2); and Article 186, paragraph 1 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, the judgment is as follows:

1. The civil judgment (2010) Hu Gao Min Si (Hai) Zhong Zi No. 71 of the Shanghai High People's Court is set aside;

2. Item 1 of the civil judgment (2009) Hu Hai Fa Shang Chu Zi No. 243 of the Shanghai Maritime Court is set aside, and it is amended as follows: Shanghai Mingri International Ship Services Co., Ltd. shall, within ten days from the date this judgment takes effect, pay ACE EUROPEAN GROUP LIMITED USD 46,094.98 for cargo damage and interest on such amount (calculated at the People's Bank of China's published USD demand deposit interest rate for enterprises for the corresponding period, from January 22, 2009, to the date this judgment takes effect);

3. Item 2 of the civil judgment (2009) Hu Hai Fa Shang Chu Zi No. 243 of the Shanghai Maritime Court is affirmed.

If Shanghai Mingri International Ship Services Co., Ltd. fails to pay the monetary obligation within the period specified in this judgment, it shall, in accordance with Article 229 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, pay double the interest on the debt for the period of delayed performance.

The court fee of first instance in the amount of RMB 8,990.75 shall be borne by ACE EUROPEAN GROUP LIMITED in the amount of RMB 2,951.33 and by Shanghai Mingri International Ship Services Co., Ltd. in the amount of RMB 6,039.42. The court fee of second instance in the amount of RMB 8,990.75 shall be borne by ACE EUROPEAN GROUP LIMITED in the amount of RMB 534.47 and by Shanghai Mingri International Ship Services Co., Ltd. in the amount of RMB 8,456.28.

This judgment is final.
